hook: Myth: selling when the market crashes protects your money.

blocks.narration: Myth: selling when the market crashes protects your money. Fact: it is one of the most expensive mistakes investors make.
blocks.visual: A clay figure clutches a money bag and leaps out of a roller coaster car at the lowest dip

blocks.narration: Here is why. The market's best days tend to show up right next to its worst days, often within the same few weeks.
blocks.visual: A jagged clay line chart where a huge drop is followed almost immediately by a tall spike

blocks.narration: When panic hits and you sell, you usually miss the sharp rebound that comes right after. Then you buy back in higher.
blocks.visual: The clay figure watches from the ground as the coaster car shoots back up without them

blocks.narration: J.P. Morgan has shown that missing just ten of the best days over twenty years can cut your overall return roughly in half.
blocks.visual: Ten glowing golden tiles are pulled out of a long path, leaving the path broken and shorter

blocks.narration: Ten days, out of roughly five thousand trading days. Nobody can reliably predict which ten days those will be.
blocks.visual: A huge wall calendar with thousands of squares, ten of them flickering briefly then vanishing

blocks.narration: That is why many long-term investors keep buying on a schedule and simply stay invested through the scary headlines.
blocks.visual: A calm clay figure drops a coin in a jar every month while storm clouds swirl overhead

blocks.narration: Volatility is the price of admission for stock returns. The people who stay seated through the dips are the ones who collect them.
blocks.visual: The roller coaster reaches a sunny summit, the calm figure still seated and smiling

blocks.narration: Time in the market tends to beat timing the market. Comment if you have ever sold at the bottom. You are not alone.
blocks.visual: Camera pulls back from the coaster track as it winds upward into golden light

cta: Comment if you have ever sold at the bottom. You are not alone.

captions.hook_line: Selling when markets crash can cut your returns in half. Here's why 📉📈
captions.body: Many of the market's best days arrive within weeks of its worst. J.P. Morgan's research has shown that missing just a handful of top days over decades sharply lowers long-term returns.
